## Traditional Indonesian Food to Try in Bali

Before we get into the best places to eat, here are some of the must-try traditional foods in Bali!

1. **Nasi Goreng and Mie Goreng** : These are iconic Indonesian dishes, consisting of fried rice (Nasi Goreng) or fried noodles (Mie Goreng). They are often mixed with vegetables, meat, and spices, sometimes topped with an egg.
2. **Babi Guling** : Also known as suckling pig, this Balinese specialty is roasted whole pig stuffed with a mixture of turmeric, coriander seeds, lemongrass, black pepper, garlic, and ginger, resulting in a flavorful and crispy dish.
3. **Ayam Betutu** : Another traditional Balinese dish is Ayam Betutu. It is chicken stuffed with traditional spices, wrapped in banana leaves, and slowly cooked until tender and flavorful.

Your itinerary

DurationHalf day
PaceBalanced, with walking and a private transfer between areas
Best forConditions vary by season; mornings are generally a comfortable time for outdoor walking. Check the local forecast before setting out.
ThemesCulture, Food

Trip overview

A balanced half-day journey from the rice terraces of Tegallalang into central Ubud, combining landscape, everyday food traditions, and a relaxed cultural walk.

Rice-terrace landscapeSee how steep terrain is shaped for wet-rice cultivation while walking along uneven, sometimes exposed paths.
Balinese flavorsEnjoy a local meal built around rice, vegetables, and spiced accompaniments, linking the surrounding farmland with daily food traditions.
Ubud cultural walkExplore a quieter selection of lanes, craft areas, and temple surroundings without focusing on the town’s nightlife.

Your day route

Tegallalang Rice Terraces

Walk the terraced paths and viewing areas to understand how Balinese farmers shape the steep landscape for wet-rice cultivation; arrive in the morning for a calmer, cooler experience.

Travel from Tegallalang toward Ubud while the route shifts from working farmland to village streets and arts-focused neighborhoods.

Makan di warung lokal sekitar Tegallalang, Ubud, Bali

Choose a local meal featuring rice, vegetables, and spiced accompaniments to connect the terrace landscape with the everyday food traditions it supports.

Ubud cultural walk

Explore a quieter selection of central Ubud lanes, craft studios, and temple surroundings to see how artistic practice and community life shape the town without entering its nightlife scene.

Know before you go

What to bring5 items

  • Comfortable walking shoes with good grip
  • Sun protection
  • Water
  • Light rain protection
  • A small bag for personal essentials

Included3 items

  • A half-day route connecting Tegallalang and Ubud
  • A local lunch
  • Walking-based sightseeing focused on terraces and cultural surroundings

Not included3 items

  • Private-car or hired-driver costs unless arranged separately
  • Personal purchases and optional activities
  • Accommodation

Local notes3 items

  • Terrace paths can be uneven, so choose secure shoes rather than open or smooth-soled footwear.
  • Dress and behave respectfully near temple surroundings, and follow local guidance about where visitors may walk or take photographs.
  • A private car or hired driver helps keep the route continuous and flexible between Tegallalang and Ubud.

Emergency contacts2 items

  • Local emergency assistance
  • Medical assistance

Travel with confidence.

This half-day route offers a practical introduction to the connection between Ubud’s landscape, food, and community life, with enough flexibility to adapt to local conditions.
